bulk.challenge:
OPEN CHALLENGE (2026-08-20, literature review; AUTHOR RULING REQUIRED). Three independent results bear on whether the bulk can be 26D at signature (24,2). They are recorded here so the ruling can be made on the evidence rather than silently reverted.

1. LATTICE OBSTRUCTION (a theorem; verified by direct computation). An even unimodular lattice of signature (p,q) exists iff p - q = 0 mod 8. For (24,2): 24 - 2 = 22 = 6 mod 8, so NO even self-dual lattice exists and there is no modular-invariant lattice compactification in this signature. By the same test (25,1) gives 24 = 0 mod 8 (the Lorentzian Leech lattice II_25,1, which bosonic string theory actually uses) and (26,2) gives 24 = 0 mod 8. Both alternatives pass; the adopted signature is the one that fails.

2. CRITICAL DIMENSION. Bars & Kounnas (hep-th/9705205, PRD 56 3664) state that the TWO-TIME bosonic critical dimension is 27 or 28, at signature (25,2) or (26,2) - adding a second time RAISES the critical dimension. Corroborated by hep-th/0308206 (consistent bosonic string in 26+2 = 28D). The familiar D_crit = 26 belongs to the ONE-time string at signature (25,1), where 26 = 24 + 2 is 24 transverse plus a LIGHTCONE PAIR (one space + one time), NOT two times. So 'D_bulk = D_crit = b3 + 2 = 26' and 'signature (24,2)' come from two different theories and cannot both be asserted while also citing Bars for ghost control.

3. SHADOW COUNTING. Bars' Sp(2,R) gauging removes exactly two dimensions: (d,2) -> d with signature (d-1,1). Applied to (24,2) it yields ONE 24D shadow of signature (23,1), not two 13D(12,1) shadows. Further, Bars' 'shadows' are different gauge-fixings of the SAME bulk - all of dimension d, related by dualities - not a partition of the bulk into halves. The framework's shadows are a different construction that reuses the word, and therefore do not inherit Bars' ghost-freedom theorem.

RESOLUTION OPTIONS (author's call): (a) (25,1), 26D, one time - matches the bosonic critical dimension and the Leech lattice, but abandons two-time. (b) (26,2), 28D, two times - matches Bars & Kounnas and passes the lattice test, but breaks 26 = b3 + 2 (it would need b3 + 4). (c) (24,2), 26D as adopted - keeps b3 + 2 and the two-time elegance, but must then drop the D_crit = 26 claim, drop the appeal to Bars for ghost-freedom, and answer the lattice obstruction independently.

Also flagged: the '+2' currently carries THREE inconsistent readings across the framework's own formulas - a lightcone pair (critical-dimension; the standard and correct reading), 'two-time (1) + Euclidean bridge (1)' (central-charge-unitarity), and '2 Sp(2,R)' (weyl-anomaly-cancellation). At most one can be right.

NOTE: beacon.two_time_bulk_accounting is integer-exact BY CONSTRUCTION and therefore cannot test any of the above - it checks internal bookkeeping, not physics.
bulk.resolution_evidence:
RESOLUTION EVIDENCE (2026-08-20, four-agent literature review). The author proposed a structure independently - 4 faces x 3 pins x 2 shadows = 24 pins, plus 2 shared 'breathing' pins, plus one time current per shadow - and it counts to signature (26,2), 28D, partitioning as 13 + 13 + 2. That option now has theorem-grade support and OPTION (b) IS RECOMMENDED:

* LATTICE DERIVES THE PARTITION. II_26,2 exists, is unique, and decomposes as Leech(24) + II_1,1 + II_1,1 (Sun & Wang arXiv:2111.10999, verbatim 'II_26,2 = 2U + Lambda'). Regrouped: (12 Leech + 1 time) + (12 Leech + 1 time) + (2 spacelike) = (12,1) + (12,1) + (2,0) = (26,2). So b3 = 24 = Leech rank, one time per shadow = one hyperbolic plane per shadow, and the two 'breathing pins' = the spacelike partners of the two times. What the framework currently ASSERTS, (26,2) largely DERIVES. Nothing comparable exists at (24,2), where the lattice does not exist at all.

* ANOMALY GIVES 28 EXACTLY. Bars & Kounnas (hep-th/9705205) eq. 41-46: c_ghost(h) = -12h^2 + 12h - 2, so h=2 gives -26 and h=1 gives -2, and c_tot = d - 28 = 0 => d = 28. Lightcone confirms 24 transverse oscillators = b3. Independently reproduced by Watabiki (hep-th/0303045) via a different route. '26 = critical dimension' returns as the DERIVED statement 28 - 2 = 26.

* MAJORANA-WEYL BECOMES AVAILABLE. (26,2) has (s-t) mod 8 = 0 and admits MW spinors (8192 real); (24,2) has 6 mod 8 and admits none. This is the same 0-mod-8 condition as the lattice test, not a second coincidence.

* SPINOR FACTORIZATION IS EXACT. Weyl Cl(26,2) = 8192 = 64 x 64 x 2 (shadow x shadow x shared sector); equivalently Dirac 16384 = 128 x 128 with one breathing pin absorbed per shadow. The cherished 4096 is not lost - it is the shadow-pair spinor, and the shared sector supplies the factor 2 that lifts it to the bulk Weyl. Under (24,2) 4096 had to serve as both bulk Weyl and shadow tensor, leaving the shared sector nowhere to live.

* SPINOR REALITY TYPES DISCRIMINATE THE SIGNATURES (derived 2026-08-20, not from the literature). Cl(12,1) has (s-t) = 11 = 3 mod 8, so each shadow's spinors are QUATERNIONIC/SYMPLECTIC - the framework's own audit already recorded 'symplectic only, no Majorana'. Two consequences. (i) An anti-linear conjugation on symplectic spinors squares to -1, so R_perp^2 = -I is FORCED by the shadow signature rather than chosen - and that is exactly the algebraic type a Tomita-Takesaki modular conjugation J would carry if it acted on the shadow spinor bundle. (ii) By Frobenius-Schur, quaternionic (x) quaternionic = REAL, so the shadow PAIR must be real. The bulk at (26,2) is real (0 mod 8, Majorana-Weyl) - CONSISTENT. The bulk at (24,2) is complex (6 mod 8) - INCONSISTENT with its own shadow decomposition. The current signature therefore fails a consistency test generated by the framework's own 13D(12,1) shadow claim.

* SPINOR REALITY TYPES DISCRIMINATE THE SIGNATURES (derived 2026-08-20, not taken from the literature). Cl(12,1) has (s-t) = 11 = 3 mod 8, so each shadow's spinors are QUATERNIONIC/SYMPLECTIC - the framework's own audit already recorded 'symplectic only, no Majorana'. Two consequences. (i) An anti-linear conjugation on symplectic spinors squares to -1, so R_perp^2 = -I is FORCED by the shadow signature rather than chosen - and that is exactly the algebraic type a Tomita-Takesaki modular conjugation J would carry if it acted on the shadow spinor bundle. (ii) By Frobenius-Schur, quaternionic x quaternionic = REAL, so the shadow PAIR must be real. The bulk at (26,2) is real (0 mod 8, Majorana-Weyl) - CONSISTENT. The bulk at (24,2) is complex (6 mod 8) - INCONSISTENT with its own shadow decomposition. The current signature therefore fails a consistency test generated by the framework's own 13D(12,1) shadow claim.

* MIGRATION IS CHEAP. The descent chain is untouched: shadows stay 13D(12,1), 13 - 7 (G2) = 6 -> 4; b3 = 24; 12 pins; 4 faces; 12 bridge pairs - all unchanged. What moves: D_BULK 26->28, signature, bulk spinor 4096->8192, alpha_T = D_bulk/D_string 2.6->2.8, and the identity 26 = b3 + 2 becomes 28 = b3 + 4 = b3 + 2 times + 2 breathing pins, which is the lattice decomposition rather than an unmotivated '+2'.

OPEN AFTER THE CHANGE (the dimension count does not fix these):
  - The 12+12 split of Leech is NOT given by the lattice (Leech is irreducible); it remains an extra choice. Possible lead, unverified: the complex Leech lattice is 12-dimensional over the Eisenstein integers.
  - Breaking SO(26,2) -> SO(12,1) x SO(12,1) x SO(2) discards the global Lorentz symmetry that Bars-Kounnas's construction rests on. That needs an argument.
  - In Bars-Kounnas the second time is REMOVED by gauge symmetry, not physical. Claiming two physical times inherits their dimension while rejecting their mechanism.
  - No published precedent for the 13+13+2 partition itself.

CORRECTION (2026-08-20, Leech survey). The bullet above overstated what the lattice delivers, and the fix changes the shadow dimension.

* U = II_1,1 HAS SIGNATURE (1,1) - one spacelike AND one timelike direction. You cannot peel the time off a hyperbolic plane and leave its spacelike partner behind as a separate 'breathing pin'. Handing one U to each half therefore gives TWO pieces of RANK 14 and signature (13,1): 14 + 14 = 28, (13+13, 1+1) = (26,2). The total is right but the partition is NOT 13 + 13 + 2. The lattice gives two 14D(13,1) shadows, not two 13D(12,1) shadows plus a 2D shared sector. Either adopt (13,1)+(13,1), or supply a separate argument for peeling one dimension off each U.

  Note this is exactly the alternative spinor reading already on record: Dirac Cl(26,2) = 16384 = 128 x 128, with Cl(13,1) Dirac = 2^7 = 128 per shadow. And 14 = dim(G2), so each shadow would carry the dimension of the holonomy group itself, with 28 = 2 x dim(G2).

* THE 12+12 SPLIT OF LEECH DOES EXIST, but not via the Eisenstein route. The complex Leech lattice IS rank 12 over Z[omega] (Wilson 1983, automorphism group 6.Suz), but omega is defined as a FIXED-POINT-FREE order-3 automorphism, so Leech^omega = 0 and there is no invariant real 12-dimensional sublattice at all. That lead is dead as stated.
  What does work: Hohn & Mason (arXiv:1505.06420, J. Algebra 448) enumerate the 290 fixed-point sublattices and find EXACTLY THREE Co_0-orbits of rank-12 splits whose two halves are isometric - orbit 4 (order-3 automorphism, frame 1^6 3^6, halves = Coxeter-Todd K_12, glue index 3^6) and orbit 5 (an involution, frame 2^12, halves = sqrt2 . D_12+, glue index 2^12), plus orbit 3. Orbit 4 is the attractive one: K_12 is itself an Eisenstein lattice, so the Z[omega] flavour survives - just not by the route originally proposed.

* CAVEAT THAT MUST NOT BE PAPERED OVER: Leech is orthogonally INDECOMPOSABLE. These are finite-index sublattices L perp L' GLUED by an anti-isometry of their discriminant forms, never direct summands. The glue is what makes Leech unimodular and rootless, so treating the two halves as independent sectors discards exactly the structure that makes the lattice special. Neither half is 'half a Leech lattice': they are K_12 or sqrt2.D_12+, neither unimodular, with different discriminant groups (3^6 vs 2^12).

* 4 x 3 IS NOT A STRUCTURE ON 24. The M_24-relevant groupings are 4x6 (the MOG array: 4 GF(4) rows, 6 hexacode columns), 6x4 (sextet, stabilizer order 138240), 3x8 (trio, 64512), 12+12 (duum, M_12:2, 190080) and the exceptional 8x3 octern (L_2(7), order 168). The 4x3 array is Conway's MiniMOG, which serves M_12 and the TERNARY Golay code on 12 points - a different group, a different code, half the dimensions. Importing it into a 24-coordinate discussion conflates M_12 with M_24. Corroborating: Leech decomposes as 12x2 (C), 6x4 (H), 3x8 (O) - the group sizes are exactly dim C, H, O, and there is no 3-dimensional division algebra, so there is no algebraic route to 'groups of 3'. Also M_24 is 5-transitive hence primitive, so NO partition of the 24 points is M_24-invariant, of any shape.

* CITATION NOTE: II_26,2 = Leech + U + U does not need a 2021 preprint. Indefinite even unimodular lattices are determined by their signature (Milnor / Serre, A Course in Arithmetic ch. V), and Leech + U + U is even, unimodular, indefinite of signature (26,2), hence IS II_26,2 by classical classification. Cite that instead - it is far more solid.
bulk.tcs_obstruction:
HARD OBSTRUCTION, INDEPENDENT OF THE BULK DIMENSION (2026-08-20, found by two agents independently). The G2 manifold this framework claims to use CANNOT EXIST as a twisted connected sum.

Crowley & Nordstrom (arXiv:1211.0269, Geom. Topol. 19) Thm 1.7 gives nu(phi) = 24 for every TCS, and the Thm 1.3 parity constraint then forces b2 + b3 to be ODD. The framework claims (b2, b3) = (4, 24), so b2 + b3 = 28, EVEN - no such TCS manifold exists. Equivalently, from the standard Betti formula b2 + b3 = b3(W1) + b3(W2) + 2d1 + 2d2 + 23, the building blocks are projective so b3(Wi) is even and the total is necessarily odd.

Corroborating: b3 = 24 lies below EVERY published TCS range (Kovalev 71-155; CHNP 55-239; 2-connected >= 31). Halverson & Morrison (arXiv:1412.4123) report CHNP Table 5 spanning 47 <= b3 <= 155.

Also: 'TCS #187' appears in no published enumeration - no TCS catalogue uses serial numbers - and the framework's generating formula b3 = 2*(h11 - h21 + h31)/6 is not a theorem in G2 geometry (h^{3,1} is a Calabi-Yau FOURFOLD Hodge number; a 7-manifold has none). The repo additionally attributes #187 to CHNP in one place and to a 'Joyce classification' in another.

ESCAPE HATCH: extra-twisted connected sums (Nordstrom arXiv:1809.09083) remove the parity constraint. Moving there would require abandoning the CHNP citation and re-deriving the Betti numbers from a construction that actually admits them.

SECOND OBSTRUCTION: Nahm's theorem excludes 13D with signature (12,1) - one time with D > 11 is forbidden for spins <= 2. Bars' S-theory uses (11,2), never (12,1). This afflicts the current (24,2) framework equally, so it is not a regression; note the irony that the fix is MORE time directions. The author's 'time current is an entropy direction, not a coordinate' is the natural escape, but it is unpublished and would have to be made precise enough to show Nahm's premises fail.

DE-ESCALATION (2026-08-20, Betti-number survey). The obstruction is narrower than first stated, and the framework's SEED SURVIVES.

* b3 = 24 IS REALIZABLE. Joyce (1996) contains a compact 7-manifold with holonomy exactly G2 and (b2, b3) = (7, 24). So b3 = 24 - the framework's fundamental seed - is in no danger. What fails is only the pairing with b2 = 4, i.e. the '4 faces per shadow' reading of b2.

* (4,24) IS UNREALIZED, NOT REFUTED. It is rigorously impossible as a TWISTED CONNECTED SUM (parity), and it appears in no published table from any construction. But no general theorem excludes it: the only known topological obstructions to a compact holonomy-G2 metric are (P1) pi_1 finite, (P2) Joyce's two integral inequalities, and (P3) Baraglia's no-fibration-over-a-3-base. There is NO published lower bound on b3 beyond the trivial b3 >= 1, and the minimum realized value is b3 = 4 at (b2,b3) = (3,4) in Joyce's 252 simply-connected examples.

* THE PARITY CONSTRAINT IS TCS-SPECIFIC. Nordstrom (arXiv:1809.09083) states for extra-twisted connected sums that '(i') There is no constraint on the parity of b2(M)+b3(M)'. So moving to ETCS removes the parity argument outright - though the ~50 published ETCS examples are nearly all 2-connected with b3 >= 42 and do not reach (4,24) either.

* NEAREST REALIZABLE PAIRS, ranked by how little the framework must change:
    (7, 24)  Joyce 1996 - KEEPS b3 = 24 EXACTLY; only b2 moves 4 -> 7. Best option if b3 is the load-bearing seed, which it is.
    (4, 27)  Joyce 1996 - keeps b2 = 4; b3 shifts +3.
    (5, 26)  in both Joyce sets and simply-connected - topologically cleanest; L1 distance 3.
    (4, 19)  Joyce simply-connected - keeps b2 = 4; b3 shifts -5.

* WHY (4,24) IS AWKWARD ON TWO INDEPENDENT GRADINGS: 239 of Joyce's 252 simply-connected examples satisfy b2+b3 = 3 mod 4, and his families sit on diagonals b2+b3 in {15,19,23,27,31,...}. (4,24) gives 28 = 0 mod 4 - wrong parity for TCS and off Joyce's mod-4 grid.

* LEAD, NOT A CLAIM: if b2 moves to 7, note that 7 is already structurally present here - dim V7, dim Im(O), and the 7 Fano lines (= the 7 quaternion subalgebras of O = the associative 3-planes), with each Fano point lying on exactly 3 lines. That is a suggestive '7 faces, 3 per point' echo of the author's '4 faces, 3 pins'. It is flagged as a RESONANCE ONLY: 7 lines x 3 points = 21 incidences, which does NOT reproduce 12 pins per shadow. Do not promote this to structure without a derivation - the theta_13 look-elsewhere ruling applies.
